Sentinel Bio co-founder and managing director Joshua Monrad joins Nathan Labenz to examine the evolving biosecurity risks posed by frontier artificial intelligence and autonomous agents. Drawing on recent in-lab uplift trials and multimodal troubleshooting benchmarks, Monrad explains how emerging models are rapidly dismantling tacit-knowledge barriers in wet labs. He analyzes potential governance interventions ranging from pathogen training-data filtering to DNA synthesis screening as robotics development looms as the final physical bottleneck. With biological tools advancing toward dual-use democratization, this discussion outlines the critical time horizon left to establish robust defense regimes.
